title: Async compact session merger and heap-friendly allocator
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: The continuous-batching path currently creates many short-lived session objects and performs synchronous compaction/merge steps on the hot path. This causes scheduler CPU spikes, frequent small KV cache evictions due to fragmentation, and GC/allocator overhead on high-concurrency workloads. Goal: introduce an asynchronous session-merger that consolidates small sessions into compact shards off the hot path, and replace the current allocator pattern with a heap-friendly strategy (upgrade / tune allocator and add arena-based pooling) to reduce fragmentation and reduce latency jitter. This ticket bundles the refactor, a dependency upgrade (allocator/jemalloc bump), and a controlled rollout plan.
technical_approach:
- Add an Async Session Merger service that runs in a separate worker pool: it receives immutable session summaries and performs compaction into shard-friendly representations.
- Change continuous-batching to emit lightweight session handles instead of full session state; the KV cache readpath will consult merged shard views.
- Implement arena-based per-shard allocators with fallback to the global allocator to reduce per-request malloc/free churn.
- Upgrade allocator vendor dependency to jemalloc 6.0 (or our internal allocator backport) and expose tunables for background purging and decay time.
- Introduce a feature flag (feature.async_session_merger) and a runtime config for merger throughput and arena sizes.
- Maintain compatibility: merger produces same logical view; if disabled, runtime falls back to existing synchronous path.
migration_plan:
1) Feature-flagged rollout: ship merger behind feature.async_session_merger=false by default.
2) Canary: enable for 5% of requests in a dedicated dedicated-pool region with heavy synthetic load.
3) Gradually increase to 50%/100% after performance validation.
4) Once stable, flip default and remove old code path in a follow-up cleanup ticket.
5) For allocator upgrade, deploy to non-customer-critical clusters first and monitor memory fragmentation and OOMs closely.
rollout_plan:
- Step 0: Merge prototype branch to feature flag. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7624
- Step 1: Deploy to staging with synthetic replay (replay-id: replay/2026-02-18-session-merge).
- Step 2: Canary on low-traffic region (us-west-2-dedicated-3) for 48h.
- Step 3: Increase traffic slices: 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% over five business days (conditional on metrics).
- Rollback: feature flag off; allocator upgrade pinned to previous runtime image until memory regressions are resolved.
acceptance_criteria: P95 token generation latency regression <= 5% compared to baseline for default prompt mix
Median tail-latency (p99) reduced by >= 10% under 75th percentile load profile
KV cache eviction rate decreased by >= 20% for long-context workloads (context > 8k tokens)
Scheduler CPU for batching/broker threads reduced by >= 15% measured under the synthetic replay
No increase in OOM incidents across canary hosts; memory fragmentation metric improved (RSS delta < 10%)

Memory fragmentation (RSS vs allocated heap), background purge frequency
risks: Allocator upgrade introduces different fragmentation characteristics or ABI incompatibilities; need canary and fast rollback.
Merger introduces eventual consistency window for newly written sessions; must ensure correctness for read-after-write semantics where required.
Feature flag complexity could increase code paths; must ensure adequate test coverage to avoid logic drift.
Underprovisioned merger worker pool could become a new bottleneck if tunables are misconfigured.
Metrics false-positives during warmup (initial evictions while arenas prime) — need burn-in period for measurements.
